lots.what_it_is: 18ct yellow gold ring with a white gold four-claw head set with a princess cut diamond, sold with an ADGL report H22439 (25/11/2011: 1.04ct princess, H colour, I1 clarity, cut proportion Good, symmetry Very Good, polish Very Good, inscribed ADGL H22439 & michael hill) and a Michael Hill certificate of authenticity (bought 22 Aug 2015, Baldivis, retail $8,999; 18ct Y&WG princess solitaire, stone no less than 1.00ct, I colour and I2 clarity or better, hallmarked 750/michael hill/1.00).

sold.note: Page opened. Sold for $2,555, auction ended 04/06/2017 (US date, so 6 April 2017, not 4 June as the researcher had). 1.04ct princess H VS1 in a 14k bridal set with extra small diamonds. Better clarity than lot 872 (VS1 vs I1), more than 9 years old and US, so a weak guide only and too old to set a bid. AUD at 1.3222.

Page opened. 1.05ct ROUND brilliant H I1, Excellent cut, 18k solitaire, 8.69g, sold $2,628, ended 09/27/2018. Same colour and clarity but round, which normally sells higher per carat than princess. 8 years old and US: category guide only, cannot set a bid. AUD at 1.3838.

lots.guide_summary: Only two SOLD results survive, both old US Worthy sales (2017 and 2018) that I opened: 1.04ct princess H VS1 bridal set USD 2,555 (AUD 3,378) and 1.05ct round H I1 solitaire USD 2,628 (AUD 3,637). No unsold or asking entries survive. No Australian or recent sale of a 1ct I1 princess was found (Gowans API searched for princess, 1ct, solitaire: nothing comparable). Both are too old (over 24 months) and too far away to set a bid. Rate used: USD 1 = AUD 1.447 (ECB via frankfurter.app, 15 Oct 2026); historic sales converted at the rate for the sale date (1.3838 on 27 Sep 2018, 1.3222 on 6 Apr 2017).
lots.working: No SOLD evidence within the last 24 months for the same item, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For context only: the old Worthy sales at AUD 3,378 to 3,637 would imply a keep ceiling of about 3,378 / 1.22 = 2,768 hammer, but they are 8 to 9 years old, US, and better clarity or a dearer shape, so they cannot be used. Inbound freight $0 (local pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).
lots.confidence_reason: The paperwork is read clearly in the photos (ADGL H22439, 1.04ct H I1), but the stone inscription is not seen, so the papers are not proven to match the stone. Price evidence is two old US sales only; no recent Australian sold result.

Allurez 4093703 (ASKING): page opened but no price on it (price field 0), loose stone not a ring, claimed currency unclear: dropped. lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 1-2: yellow gold band with a white gold four-claw (V-corner) head holding a single princess cut stone, in a purple Michael Hill style box, looks clean and bright with no visible damage. Photos 3-4: Michael Hill certificate of authenticity, stock code 11339731, 18ct Y&WG princess solitaire, no less than 1.00ct, I colour and I2 or better, hallmark 750/michael hill/1.00, purchased 22 Aug 2015, retail $8,999. Photo 5: ADGL report H22439 dated 25/11/2011, princess, 1.04ct, 5.19 x 5.40 mm approx, depth 80.5%, table 70.9%, cut proportion GOOD (researcher wrote VG/VG, which is symmetry and polish only), colour H, clarity I1, inscribed ADGL H22439 & michael hill. Hallmark on the shank and the girdle inscription are not shown.
lots.condition: Appears very good from the photos, claws intact, no obvious wear shown. Shank hallmark and girdle inscription not seen. I1 clarity means inclusions may be visible to the eye.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the shank is hallmarked 750 / michael hill / 1.00, and can the girdle inscription ADGL H22439 be seen under a loupe so the report matches the stone? Are the claws all tight, any chips to the corners of the princess stone, and what does the ring weigh? Is the 'valuation' in the description the Michael Hill certificate only, or is there a separate insurance valuation?

lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD hammer results at Gowans, Hobart (Jan to Sep 2026), opened as individual API lot records: plain 9ct bangles made $46.8 to $64.9/g hammer (4.6g $280, 11.1g $720, 15.5g $725, 18g $1,150) and 9ct bracelets and chains $60.5 to $69.5/g. Scaled to the catalogued 34.8g that is about $1,628 to $2,418 hammer (raw prices $280 to $2,950). No unsold or asking entries survive. All AUD, no conversion. Gold melt not checked (goldprice.org returned Forbidden), so no melt floor is stated.
lots.working: Same-item SOLD = Gowans plain 9ct bangles in the last 24 months, scaled by weight to 34.8g. Lowest = 15.5g at $725 = $46.8/g x 34.8 = $1,628. keep_max = 1,628 / 1.22 = $1,334, rounded down to $1,330 (all-in $1,622.60). Flip: likely resale from the most recent bangle rate $60.9/g (Sep 2026) x 34.8 = $2,118 hammer at Gowans; less an assumed 15% seller commission ($318) and $0 outbound postage (local room) = $1,800; / 2.44 = $738, rounded down to $735. Inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). Both figures depend entirely on the 34.8g weight being right and the bangle being solid 9ct, not lined or filled.
lots.confidence_reason: The 375 stamp is legible on enlargement and there are several opened Tasmanian SOLD results, but the 34.8g weight cannot be checked from one photo and construction (solid versus lined or filled) is unconfirmed. 34.8g is heavy for a hollow bangle of this size, which is reassuring but not proof.
lots.dropped_entries: Gowans 391711 (3 scrap gold items incl 9ct bangle, 17.4g, $1,200): confirmed in the API but it is a mixed scrap lot, left out as not the same item. Lawsons via Invaluable 'antique 9ct gold-lined bangle' (filed by the researcher as ASKING with an estimate midpoint): snippet only, and it is a gold-lined (base metal) hinged bangle, not the same item; an estimate on a sold lot is neither an ask nor a price paid. Dropped, but kept in mind as a warning about lined bangles. eBay.de 167888973422 (ASKING AU$2,924.96): eBay is closed to us, snippet only, title and weight not seen: dropped. Researcher's 'url' strings were search URLs with lot ids in brackets; replaced with the individual lot record URLs that I opened.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Plain flat-section bangle, even width, slightly bevelled edges, no hinge or clasp so a slip-on. Enlarged crop of the inner face shows a small '375' stamp (legible); a faint second mark just above it may be a maker's mark but is not readable. No 'gold lined', 'RG' or '1/5' type mark visible. General light surface scratching, colour even with no base metal showing at the edges.
lots.condition: Good used, light surface wear and scratches, no dents or splits visible in the one photo. Weight and solidity not verifiable from the photo.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the 34.8g weight on scales, and that the bangle is solid 9ct (not gold-lined or filled), with any marks beside the 375 stamp? Any dents, splits or solder repairs?
